messages:
Nora: Quick heads-up: doing initial bring-up for orchid-v2 (fp16 -> q5) on staging. Found deterministic detok spacing problem for CJK + Arabic spans. Short thread with examples and logs below.
Taro: paste sample?
Nora: example:
```
INPUT: 日本語とالعربية are mixed here.
EXPECTED (fp16 reference): 日本語と العربية are mixed here.  -- space between CJK and RTL word, Arabic on the right
FP16 OUTPUT: 日本語と العربية are mixed here.
Q5 OUTPUT: 日本語と2742c27284a29 are mixed here.  <-- punctuation/space glued to CJK; Arabic rendered but no separator
```
Lina: ugh. tokenization changed or detok heuristics flipped? Most of these are detok postprocessing issues. Any token id diffs?
Nora: token-id diffs look benign for this sample. Ran a batch compare on our mixed-orient smoke (2k samples) and saw a localized quality hit: zh->ar BLEU -0.9; zh->ar punctuation-spacing metric up 18% (more adjacency failures) on q5 vs fp16.
Ben: Could be locale resolution. Our detok uses profiles loaded from /etc/redwood/locale_profiles.json at startup. If the q5 runtime chroot/chdir changes, relative paths break. Any relevant logs?
Nora: found this in the canary logs for orchid-v2@d4e5f6: 
```
2026-03-22T20:03:11Z orchid-init: tokenizer v3 loaded
2026-03-22T20:03:11Z quant-runtime: q5 kernels ready
2026-03-22T20:03:11Z profile-loader: open("./profiles/locale_profiles.json") -> ENOENT
2026-03-22T20:03:11Z detok: profile missing, using generic-join fallback
```
Priya: So the fp16 build probably uses absolute path and q5 build ended up with relative. We had one change in the quant bootstrap that alters cwd for memory mapping reasons. That would explain why the profile-loader can't find the file under q5.
Taro: Is the fallback actually harmful? generic-join will just concatenate tokens and that breaks spacing for CJK+RTL. We need the locale-specific glue rules.
Ben: Agreed. Fix plan: 1) change profile-loader to resolve to an absolute path (server config absolute on startup) 2) include a sanity check in the model bring-up e2e smoke to run a tiny detok assertion (sample 500 mix-orient pairs) 3) add unit test that simulates missing cwd to prevent regressions.
Lina: I'll open PR for profile-loader patch and a test. @Ben can you add the e2e detok check to the onboarding checklist?
Ben: Yep. Adding a CI job: infra-bot, please queue a detok sanity job for orchid-q5 canary.
infra-bot: Queued job: ci/detok_sanity/orchid-q5-2026-03-22 #998. Logs will appear here: https://ci.internal/runs/998 :rocket:
Nora: For tracking created ML ticket ML-3510 with a few failing sample ids and diffs. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-3510
Priya: Small note: there was also a perf micro-optimization in the quant init that munges env.CWD for child processes. We should root-cause that separately; for now absolute path fix is safest.
Taro: Suggest add an automated metric to our shadow-eval: "CJK-RTL separator rate" (fraction of CJK->RTL adjacency with at least one whitespace or zero-width joiner). Fail bring-up if drop > 5% vs baseline.
Lina: Good call. I'll add that metric to the bring-up dashboard and the canary smoke.
Nora: Action items captured: @Lina PR to profile-loader and unit test, @Ben add detok-sanity to onboarding CI, @Taro add metric to shadow-eval dashboard, @Priya investigate quant init CWD change. We'll pause broad rollout until ci/detok_sanity passes.
Ben: I'll also roll a quick shadow canary with profile path forced absolute to confirm no other surprises.
Nora: Thanks all — will post CI outcomes here when job finishes. :thumbsup:
